prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Generate a scene-state sheet with SIX equal SQUARE scenes, THREE columns and TWO rows. This is INSIDE the compact cream-riveted ascent cabin of reference 1, looking toward its rear cargo wall, not at an exterior hull. Consistent realistic painterly expedition equipment style. Repeat EXACTLY the same camera, framing, light and hardware across all six cells; only sample contents change. No text, labels, arrows, numbers, people or diagram. Inside the cabin, a small built-in cobalt-and-metal refrigerated rack occupies the LEFT half of the wall, with TWO clearly separate horizontal core chambers stacked vertically, each with a fitted cradle, two retaining clips and its own clear observation face. A much SMALLER square specimen locker is on the RIGHT wall, clearly separate from the refrigerated rack. It is sized for the thin sealed membrane holder in reference 4. Existing cabin machinery, rivets and a small edge of the pilot seat establish that we are inside the spacecraft. No outdoor ground, exterior lander view, external cargo door, open air or separate portable laboratory. Show only practical installed hardware at human cabin scale. Leave the bottom third simple metal cabin floor for draggable items. The core cylinders are the actual objects in references 2 and 3: the SOURCE core has scattered brown flecks in pale ice, while the REMOTE core has one distinct brown sediment band through the ice, both in blue-end sealed transparent liners. Never mix the two. The membrane is the square thin cobalt-edged holder containing scattered tiny ambiguous brown fragments, not an intact animal.
STATE 1 top-left: both core cradles empty; small membrane locker empty.
STATE 2 top-middle: source core secured in UPPER left cradle only; lower cradle and right locker empty.
STATE 3 top-right: remote brown-band core secured in LOWER left cradle only; upper cradle and right locker empty.
STATE 4 bottom-left: both core cradles empty; membrane holder secured inside RIGHT small locker only.
STATE 5 bottom-middle: source core secured upper, remote core secured lower; right membrane locker empty.
STATE 6 bottom-right: both correct cores secured in their respective cradles AND membrane secured in right locker.
Each complete core stays inside its sealed liner with its surrounding ice, attached to flight cooling through its cradle. Keep all chamber dimensions, clips, perspective, walls and shadows identical. All required slots clearly visible and distinct, full silhouettes inside frame.
